name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS)
description: A large multilingual corpus suitable for speech research derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox. The dataset consists of 8 languages, including about 44.5K hours of English and a total of about 6K hours for other languages (German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, Polish).

creator.name: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert

inLanguage: en, de, nl, es, fr, pt, it, pl
citeAs: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert. MLS: A Large-Scale Multilingual Dataset for Speech Research. arXiv:2012.03411v2 [eess.AS], December 22, 2020.
rai:dataCollection: Audio data was downloaded from LibriVox audiobooks using data preparation tools from LibriLight open source library. All audio data was downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz. Text sources were downloaded from multiple domains including gutenberg.org, archive.org, ccel.org, and hathitrust.org for English, with manual approaches incorporated for other languages to extract text from various domains, PDFs, and EPUBs.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Read audiobooks from LibriVox and corresponding text sources from Project Gutenberg and other public domain sources. For acoustic model training used for segmentation and pseudo-labeling, in-house datasets consisting of audio from videos publicly shared by users were used (completely de-identified).
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Numbers in text were replaced with corresponding aligned words from pseudo labels. Heuristics were applied to deal with hyphens and apostrophes, including removing end-of-line hyphenation and replacing rare words with hyphens or apostrophes based on frequency thresholds.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio files were segmented into 10-20 second segments using trained acoustic models with Time-Depth Separable (TDS) Convolutions and Auto-Segmentation Criterion (ASG) loss. Segmentation was performed by generating viterbi token sequences with timestamps and splitting at silence intervals. Text normalization included NFKC normalization, removal of unwanted characters (punctuations, subscripts/superscripts, emojis, escape symbols), removal of end-of-line hyphens, and filtering characters outside valid unicode ranges based on language orthography.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Transcripts were retrieved by generating pseudo-labels using beam-search decoding with 4-gram language models on acoustic models, then matching pseudo-labels to book transcripts using TF-IDF similarity on bigrams and Smith-Waterman alignment (matching score 2, substitution/insertion/deletion score -1). Candidate transcripts with WER >40% between pseudo-label and matched text were filtered out. For development and test sets, human transcribers listened to audio while reviewing transcripts and corrected clear and obvious errors only.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Candidate transcripts were filtered if WER between pseudo-label and matched text exceeded 40%. Human verification was performed on development and test sets, with WER between generated and human-rated transcripts ranging from 1.93% to 12.64% across languages.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Acoustic models using Time-Depth Separable (TDS) Convolutions with Auto-Segmentation Criterion (ASG) loss for segmentation. Beam-search decoding with 4-gram language models for pseudo-label generation. wav2letter@anywhere framework for streaming inference. TF-IDF for document matching. Smith-Waterman alignment algorithm for transcript retrieval.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Gender information was collected for speakers using a gender classifier (SVM with RBF kernel trained on LibriSpeech data, achieving 95% test accuracy). Development and test sets were balanced by gender and duration.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is read-speech only, derived from audiobooks. For English, speakers with WER higher than 80% of dev-other sets were selected for MLS dev/test sets to create harder evaluation sets. Polish language has high OOV rate (13.39%) which negatively impacts WER when performing LM decoding with constrained lexicon. Text sources for some audiobooks were unavailable due to invalid links or domain diversity, requiring manual search for alternate sources.
rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation. The dataset is suitable for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) research and Text-To-Speech (TTS) research. Limited supervision datasets are provided (10 hour, 1 hour, and six 10-minute sets) for low-resource training benchmarks. The dataset can be used for large-scale training of ASR systems and multilingual ASR research.
